To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stroke lesions and rehabilitation can induce changes in brain connectivity that are related to functional recovery and that these changes can be measured using different neuroimaging techniques.

ischemic stroke impairs motor function by affecting motor network connectivity and that the reorganization and plasticity of this connectivity is an important mechanism of motor recovery after ischemic stroke.

ischemic stroke induces changes in connectivity among motor areas that are associated with the degree of motor impairment and that therapeutic interventions may influence the connectivity among motor areas and facilitate motor recovery after ischemic stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) the relationship between motor impairment and brain plasticity; (2) the relationship between functional connectivity changes and motor recovery; (3) the relationship between effective connectivity changes and motor impairment; (4) the relationship between connectivity changes and therapeutic interventions.
the development of a novel, efficient and robust approach to the problem of brain connectivity in the context of stroke recovery.
the mechanisms of motor impairment and recovery after stroke.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stroke-induced motor impairment is associated with changes in connectivity among motor areas and that these changes may contribute to functional recovery after stroke.
the motor function is controlled via a network of cortical and sub-cortical regions, which are anatomically interconnected and interact functionally.
stroke-induced changes in brain network connectivity can be used for outcome prediction and for the design of treatment strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain connectivity plasticity in the motor network after stroke is a critical factor for the motor recovery and the treatment strategies.
the connectivity of the motor areas is altered after stroke and these changes are associated with the motor recovery.
connectivity changes constitute a fundamental aspect of the pathophysiology of motor impairment and recovery after stroke and thus should be included in the future research of stroke recovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the connectivity among the brain areas is an important pathophysiology and therapeutic target for stroke.
the motor system is not a static network but rather a dynamic network that is able to adapt to the changes in its structure and function after stroke.
connectivity analyses improved our knowledge of the mechanisms of recovery after stroke and that they can be used to design more hypothesis-driven treatment strategies.
